title: The four markets redefining Africa upstream
gist: Wood Mackenzie's Ian Thom frames Sub-Saharan Africa's upstream recovery around four markets: Nigeria and Angola regaining momentum on fiscal reform and project approvals, with Namibia and Mozambique emerging as frontier growth stories on world-class discoveries and LNG. The written page is only a short trailer for a 4:59 video, so the argument is asserted rather than evidenced — no production, capex or project-level numbers are given in the text.

insights.claim: Nigeria and Angola, Sub-Saharan Africa's two largest legacy oil producers, are showing strong signs of growing upstream momentum rather than continued decline.
insights.speaker: Ian Thom
insights.so_what: A genuine turn in the two biggest African producers would re-rate service demand and licence-round interest across the region; watch Nigerian and Angolan FIDs for confirmation.
insights.quote: Nigeria and Angola are showing strong signs of growing upstream momentum
insights.locator: Nigeria and Angola are showing strong signs

insights.claim: Fiscal reforms, major project approvals and improving investment conditions are the mechanism pulling international capital back into Sub-Saharan African oil and gas.
insights.speaker: Ian Thom
insights.so_what: Policy and fiscal-terms changes, not price alone, are the leading indicator to track for African upstream capital allocation.
insights.quote: Fiscal reforms, major project approvals and improving investment conditions are attracting capital back to the region
insights.locator: Fiscal reforms, major project approvals and improving

themes.theme: Namibia and Mozambique as frontier growth stories

insights.claim: Namibia and Mozambique are emerging as two of the world's most closely watched upstream growth stories, putting frontier African acreage on the same watchlist as established basins.
insights.speaker: Ian Thom
insights.so_what: Frontier exposure via operators and partners in Namibia and Mozambique is where the optionality sits if the region's next growth phase materialises.
insights.quote: Namibia and Mozambique are emerging as two of the world's most closely watched growth stories
insights.locator: Nigeria and Angola are showing strong signs

insights.claim: World-class discoveries and LNG developments are opening new long-term opportunities in Sub-Saharan Africa, extending the investment horizon beyond near-term oil barrels.
insights.speaker: Ian Thom
insights.so_what: Long-dated LNG offtake and discovery appraisal timelines mean exposure is a multi-year hold, not a cyclical trade.
insights.quote: world-class discoveries and LNG developments are opening up new long-term opportunities
insights.locator: Fiscal reforms, major project approvals and improving

insights.claim: Ian Thom, head of regional upstream analysis for Europe, Russia, the Caspian and Africa, treats Nigeria, Angola, Namibia and Mozambique as the four markets that together reshape the outlook and competitiveness of Sub-Saharan Africa's oil and gas sector.
insights.speaker: Ian Thom
insights.so_what: Gives a compact four-country checklist for monitoring African upstream capital flows instead of tracking the whole continent.
insights.quote: Together, these four markets are reshaping the outlook for Sub-Saharan Africa's oil and gas sector.
insights.locator: In this video, we explore the four markets
